To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a next-to-leading-order QCD angular asymmetry is able to discriminate the graviton exchange against the scalar one, for masses of the resonance below 3.2 TeV.

the graviton exchange could, in principle, be distinguished from the scalar exchange with the same mass MR and the same rate in the diphotons events, up to MR=3.2 TeV, with the LHC with energy 14 TeV, luminosity 100fb−1.

1) a spin-0 resonance in diphoton events can be discriminated from the graviton one, up to MR ≃ 3.2 TeV; 2) the graviton exchange can be discriminated at LHC from a spin-2 Kaluza-Klein graviton excitation with same mass, up to MR = 1.6 TeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the quantum numbers of a diphotons resonance by a simple angular analysis of the associated events at the Lhc, in the context of a model-independent approach.
the spin determination of a diphotons resonance at the LHC, in the context of the Randall-Sundrum model, where the graviton is the only mediator of gravity between the TeV and Planck scales.
the study of the angular distribution of the final state particles in the diphotons production process, with the aim of discriminating between different spin assignments for the s-channel resonance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the graviton exchange can be excluded at the 3σ level, while the scalar exchange can be excluded with 2σ significance.
, in the presence of a s-channel diphotons resonance with mass below 3.2 TeV, the graviton exchange could not be the only source of the signal.
a graviton exchange can be discriminated against a scalar one with same events rate, up the MR≃2TeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a spin-2 resonance can be identified by the LHC at the same mass as a spin-0 one, provided the latter is not much heavier than 3TeV.
the angular-integrated asymmetries are sensitive to the quantum numbers of the diphoton resonance and thus provide a powerful tool to determine them, and hence the underlying New Physics, at the LHC.

, in the case of a diphotons resonance with a mass of a few TeV, a spin analysis of the events would be crucial to discriminate between the two competing models, the RS graviton and a heavy scalar, and would allow to probe the spin-2 graviton exchange in a region of the parameter space which is still unexplored by the LHC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin-2 graviton exchange can be identified at the LHC by a simple angular-integrated asymmetries in the diphotons events.
the spin of the diphoton resonance can be inferred with high accuracy, and thus the nature of New Physics, by a single angular-integrated asymmetrical distribution.
the spin of the s-channel resonance can be determined by the LHC with a reasonable precision, provided that the mass of the resonance is not too large.
